meta.gift: warmth, disparity, and the colour of souls
meta.waning: the Ember gutters; shadows lengthen and the dead forget to lie down
meta.curse_desc: a grey brand that spreads over the heart; the marked wander until their names burn out
veils: The rites of rekindling consume souls faster than the Ember returns them, and the church keeps the arithmetic hidden.
The Ember is not dying — the gods siphon it to prolong their reign, and the curse is the siphon's residue.
The siphon was the Ember's own bargain: it feeds the gods so that something older, asleep in its heart, stays asleep. The gods know, and keep feeding.
meta.epigraph: Herein lie the things the dead would not put down. Read them one against another, for no keeper tells the whole of it, and the Ember keeps its own counsel.

ages.name: the Age of the Gift
ages.blurb: the First Ember gave the world warmth, disparity, and the colour of souls.

ages.name: the Age of Names
ages.blurb: The gods withdrew to their high seats and mortals learned to matter. Then the waning began: the Ember gutters; shadows lengthen and the dead forget to lie down.

ages.name: the Age of Dusk
ages.blurb: The present age. The gods are silent, the roads belong to the marked, and pilgrims walk toward rumours of a cure.

e1.text: the First Ember rose (or was raised — the tellings differ) and gave the world warmth, disparity, and the colour of souls.

e2.text: Athara, god of storms and unkept promises, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e3.text: Calmund, god of craft, measure, and the forge, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e4.text: Calanos, god of law, chains, and the first covenant, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e6.text: The Pyre of Athara was wrought as regalia of Athara's throne.

e8.text: The Pyre of Calmund was wrought as regalia of Calmund's throne.

e10.text: The Ember of Calanos was wrought as regalia of Calanos's throne.

e11.text: Galott, the Cinder-Eater, rose against the thrones. Athara led the gods to war.
e11.hidden: Calanos treated with Galott in secret and was spared what followed.

e12.text: Galott was defeated and sealed beneath Omthasdeep; the seal was bought with the lives of 5 champions.

e13.text: The waning began: the Ember gutters; shadows lengthen and the dead forget to lie down. Mortals called the affliction the Gutter-mark: a grey brand that spreads over the heart; the marked wander until their names burn out.

e14.text: Ishveth the Adamant founded the Order of the Cinder at Nyuastcrown, sworn to stand against the Gutter-mark.

e15.text: The Church of Athara was raised at Karulahold; Ranach the Kindly took its first pulpit, preaching that the waning is a trial and the faithful will be spared.

e16.text: Fenenyne the Quiet was cast out of Church of Athara and founded the Cult of the Patient Below, teaching that the gods themselves caused the waning.
e16.hidden: The heresy is nearer the truth than the sermon.

e17.text: Banuldis the Adamant united the river-clans and was crowned in Torivanevault; the realm took the name Bangrimhollow.

e18.text: At the urging of Ranach, the saint Hariach the Saltborn was given to the First Ember in the rite of restoration. For a generation, the waning slowed.
e18.hidden: The rite did not restore anything. It only fed the waning more slowly — and Ranach suspected as much.

e19.text: Ishencael the Adamant, sword-hand of Banuldis, opened the gates of Torivanevault to the Order of the Cinder over a grievance no chronicle agrees on.
e19.hidden: Ishencael acted on a promise from the Cult of the Patient Below: that the marked of their house would be spared the Gutter-mark. The promise was not kept.

e20.text: Bangrimhollow fell. Banuldis the Adamant died at the foot of their own throne; the crown was carried away and never worn again.

e21.text: Ishencael was found at Nyuastcrown bearing the Gutter-mark, and was not spared.

e22.text: Calanos, god of law, chains, and the first covenant, took the Gutter-mark — the first of the gods to bear it — and wandered from their seat.
e22.hidden: The curse does not distinguish gods from mortals. It never did.

e23.text: Fenrion the Latecomer, last-sworn of the Order of the Cinder, set out for the place where Calanos was lost, carrying the order's final blessing.

e24.text: Fenrion returned once, said nothing, left their sword upon the order's altar, and walked into the dusk unarmed.

e25.text: Pilgrims of the Cult of the Patient Below were found digging at the seal of Galott. The wardens hanged nine; the digging continued.
e25.hidden: The seal has been failing on its own since the waning began. The cult only follows the cracks.

a1.name: Pyre of Athara
knowledge: (year 53) The Pyre of Athara was wrought as regalia of Athara's throne.
This item is kept/told of by Ghalorhildfen (kingdom), seat at Velvethmere.
The affliction of this world: the Gutter-mark — a grey brand that spreads over the heart; the marked wander until their names burn out.
a1.bias: courtly and proud; flatters its founders, omits their crimes
a1.description:
Regalia of the storm-god's throne, borne by the kings of Velvethmere.

Athara raised it in the first warmth, when promises were newly made and not yet broken. The court remembers only the giving. Now the grey brand creeps upon hearts that once knelt here, and the marked wander until their names burn out — yet the halls insist the storm still keeps its word.
a1.placement: Kept long at Velvethmere, and then kept poorly.

a2.name: Pyre of Calmund
knowledge: (year 71) The Pyre of Calmund was wrought as regalia of Calmund's throne.

The affliction of this world: the Gutter-mark — a grey brand that spreads over the heart; the marked wander until their names burn out.
a2.bias: courtly and proud; flatters its founders, omits their crimes
a2.description:
A forged blade-flame, regalia of Calmund's throne at Ostachhold.

Calmund, god of craft and measure, set his fire in steel and called it just. The smiths of Nimiadragate boast that nothing his hand shaped has ever failed. They do not speak of the grey mark, which measures every heart alike and asks no leave of the forge.
a2.placement: Kept long at Ostachhold, and then kept poorly.

a3.name: Ember of Calanos
knowledge: (year 110) The Ember of Calanos was wrought as regalia of Calanos's throne.
Calanos, god of law, chains, and the first covenant: fate — took the Gutter-mark and wandered (year 453).
This item is kept/told of by Hestirosshroud (kingdom), seat at Ruthornspire.
The affliction of this world: the Gutter-mark — a grey brand that spreads over the heart; the marked wander until their names burn out.
a3.bias: courtly and proud; flatters its founders, omits their crimes
a3.description:
A talisman, regalia of the covenant-god's throne at Ruthornspire.

Calanos bound law to chain, and chain to the first oath. The court still keeps his ledgers, and swears the rites return as much as they cost — though none may read the sum. In the end even the lawgiver took the grey brand and wandered from his seat. What covenant, then, was left unpaid?
a3.placement: Kept long at Ruthornspire, and then kept poorly.

knowledge: (year 154) Galott, the Cinder-Eater, rose against the thrones. Athara led the gods to war.
[half-known secret] Calanos treated with Galott in secret and was spared what followed.
(year 163) Galott was defeated and sealed beneath Omthasdeep; the seal was bought with the lives of 5 champions.

This item is kept/told of by Ghalorhildfen (kingdom), seat at Velvethmere.

a4.bias: courtly and proud; flatters its founders, omits their crimes
a4.description:
A war-blade kindled for the god's own hand.

When Galott the Cinder-Eater rose against the thrones, Athara led the gods to war, and the brand drank deep at Omthasdeep. Five champions bought the seal with their lives. It is said Calanos was spared the worst of that field, though the tellings differ on why. The proud halls name it victory, and leave the rest unspoken.
a4.placement: Worn smooth by warders' hands at Omthasdeep.

knowledge: (year 347) At the urging of Ranach, the saint Hariach the Saltborn was given to the First Ember in the rite of restoration. For a generation, the waning slowed.

a6.bias: liturgical; frames all loss as trial and all doubt as sin
a6.false_rumor: claims the relic was a gift when it was plunder
a6.description:
What remains of the saint's soul, kept in the reliquary at Karulahold.

Hariach the Saltborn gave himself freely to the Ember — so the Church tells, and so it is graven above the altar. A gift, offered with open hands, that the waning might slow a while. The faithful are taught to grieve softly and ask nothing. For a generation it held. Then the dusk returned to lengthen, and the giving was asked again.
a6.placement: Kept in a reliquary at Karulahold, before which the candles will not stay lit.

a5.name: Pyre of Saint Hariach
knowledge: (year 347) At the urging of Ranach, the saint Hariach the Saltborn was given to the First Ember in the rite of restoration. For a generation, the waning slowed.

a5.false_rumor: attributes the deed to a god who had no part in it
a5.description:
A relic-flame of the saint given to the Ember.

At Calmund's asking, Hariach the Saltborn walked into the First Ember, and for a generation the waning slowed. The Church names this mercy: a trial borne gladly, a doubt burned clean. Blessed is the one who does not ask what the fire took — nor why the slowing did not last.
a5.placement: Kept in a reliquary at Karulahold, before which the candles will not stay lit.

a7.description:
A crown carried from a fallen hall and never worn again.

Torivanevault opened in the night — some say Athara himself struck the gates, that no mortal hand could have done such a thing. Banuldis the Adamant died at the foot of his own throne. The chroniclers of Bangrimhollow keep the crown hollow, and lay the ruin at a god's door, that they need not name the sword-hand who turned.
a7.placement: Found at the foot of a throne in Bangrimhollow, beneath the dust of the banners.

a8.name: Ishencael's Oathbreaker Blade
knowledge: (year 386) Ishencael the Adamant, sword-hand of Banuldis, opened the gates of Torivanevault to the Order of the Cinder over a grievance no chronicle agrees on.

a8.false_rumor: insists the dead figure still lives, in hiding
a8.description:
The blade of the sword-hand who opened the gates.

Ishencael the Adamant let the Order of the Cinder into Torivanevault, over a grievance no chronicle names alike. The king fell — or so it was told; some swear Banuldis was borne off living, and waits yet in some hollow for the crown to be returned. The blade keeps its own counsel. It remembers a gate, and a promise, and neither fondly.
a8.placement: Found at the foot of a throne in Bangrimhollow, beneath the dust of the banners.

knowledge: (year 453) Calanos, god of law, chains, and the first covenant, took the Gutter-mark — the first of the gods to bear it — and wandered from their seat.

a9.bias: courtly and proud; flatters its founders, omits their crimes
a9.description:
The soul-remnant of the covenant-god, gathered at Ruthornspire.

Calanos was first among the gods to take the grey brand, and wandered from his high seat as any marked beggar might. The court will not say it plainly, but the mark asked no leave of his godhood. Nor did the rites ever return what they were fed — a reckoning the ledgers keep, and never show. Law, it seems, binds even the lawgiver.
a9.placement: Taken from a throne room at Ruthornspire where nothing else was disturbed.

a10.name: Fenrion's Set
knowledge: (year 487) Fenrion the Latecomer, last-sworn of the Order of the Cinder, set out for the place where Calanos was lost, carrying the order's final blessing.
(year 494) Fenrion returned once, said nothing, left their sword upon the order's altar, and walked into the dusk unarmed.

a10.bias: austere and dutiful; honours oaths, distrusts miracles
a10.description:
The armour of the last-sworn of the Order of the Cinder.

Fenrion the Latecomer went to the place where Calanos was lost, bearing the order's final blessing. He returned once, said nothing, and laid his sword upon the altar. Then he walked into the dusk unarmed. The order keeps his plate as it keeps its oaths: unpolished, and without miracle. What he saw there, he did not leave behind in words.
a10.placement: Left behind at Nyuastcrown, and never reclaimed.

a11.false_rumor: places the event a whole age too early
a11.description:
A vigil-ring of the Order of the Cinder.

It is said Fenrion the Latecomer wore this when he set out for the place where the god was lost — in the Age of Names, when the order was young and its altars full. He came back once and left his sword, then walked unarmed into the dusk. The ring keeps the vigil still. Its watch has outlasted the men who swore it.
a11.placement: Left behind at Nyuastcrown, and never reclaimed.

a12.description:
A ward-flame, blessed against what stirs below, and spent in a single kindling.

When pilgrims of the Patient Below were found digging at the seal of Galott, the wardens hanged nine, and the Church kindled these against the dark. The flame was a gift to the faithful, freely bestowed — so the pulpits say. Galott has lain sealed at Omthasdeep since the war of the gods. The digging, they add, is nothing. The digging continued.
a12.placement: Confiscated from pilgrims on the roads to the Pilgrim Roads.
